name: Addis Ababa Bole International Airport
before:
Africa's main connecting airport, and the reason so many routes between Europe and southern Africa run through Ethiopia. Ethiopian Airlines has its hub here and flies from it across the continent and on to Asia, Europe, North America and South America. By mid 2018 it was handling close to 380 flights a day.

It is close in, 6 km south east of the centre of Addis Ababa, so transfers are short.

The Ethiopian Aviation Academy is based on the site, which is part of why the airline has been able to grow at the rate it has.

One thing to keep an eye on for itineraries a few years out: a replacement hub is being built at Bishoftu, 65 km south, with completion projected for 2030. The current airport opened at Bole in the early 1960s, after the old field at Lideta proved too short for the airline's first jets.
after:
The main hub of Ethiopian Airlines, which flies from here across Africa and on to Asia, Europe and the Americas.

It is close in, about 6 km south east of central Addis Ababa, so transfers are short.

Bole is running short of capacity. One thing to keep an eye on for itineraries a few years out: work began in January 2026 on a new hub at Bishoftu, about 40 km south of Addis Ababa. Its first phase is due to open in 2030.

'About' and 'central' follow Ethiopian's wording.

claims.claim: Bole is running short of capacity
claims.inAfter: Bole is running short of capacity.
claims.note: Replaces the 2018 figure of close to 380 flights a day as the line on how busy it is. No passenger number is given because good sources disagree: 12.1 million in 2024 (Wikipedia's infobox, citing Business Insider Africa, and InsideFlyer) against 'nearly 20 million' last year (Ethiopian's chief executive, reported by Fana in September 2025). Both the airline's chief executive (Fana) and the Prime Minister (Dezeen) expect Bole to reach its limit within two to three years.

claims.note: Was 'a replacement hub is being built'. 'Replacement' is softened to 'new hub': Ethiopian's chief executive said in September 2025 that international flights would start at Bishoftu by 2030 and that Bole would be modernised for domestic flights (ENA), so Bole is not simply being replaced. That split rests on one source and is not in the text.
